answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The operator must contact MSHA immediately, and within 15 minutes, once the operator knows or should know that a death has occurred at the mine.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes once it knows or should know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is covered by this notification requirement.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent (the increase applies only where methane is present).
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent. Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: Each underground coal miner must be given an approved self-rescue device that is adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: The operator must make available to each miner going underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift, at some time other than a shift change, and must involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

claims.text: Drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties (30 CFR 48.5). Approximately 8 hours of that training is given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Approximately 8 hours of the training is given at the minesite.
claims.quote: approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA. Equivalently, it is a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. The rule reads the same in 30 CFR 56.9300 and 57.9300.

claims.text: Under 56.9300, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Under 57.9300, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address OSHA's bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan. They cover MSHA mining rules on respiratory protection and respirable dust control plans.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth an OSHA construction trench needs a protective system. They only cover MSHA mining rules: shaft sinking buckets, shaft deepening protection, coal mine slope and shaft plans, and protective clothing.
